components.css: .ds-chips { display: flex; gap: 8px; font-family: 'Segoe UI', system-ui, sans-serif; } .ds-chip { padding: 7px 14px; border-radius: 8px; border: 1px solid rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.24); background: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.05); color: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.6); font-size: 12px; cursor: pointer; transition: background 0.15s, border-color 0.15s, color 0.15s; } .ds-chip:hover { background: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.09); } .ds-chip:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #9D4EDD; outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-chip.ds-selected { background: rgba(157, 78, 221, 0.25); border-color: #9D4EDD; color: #fff; font-weight: 600; }

narrative.overview:
Sona is a physical object behind a pane of tinted glass. The record (a spinning vinyl, or the bare album cover) sits at the center of a translucent card. The glass takes its tint from the user's accent color, and the room around it is lit by the track itself: the album artwork, blurred until only its colors remain, fills the window behind everything.

The interface is discreet and refined. Controls are thin-edged, low in contrast and quiet until touched. Color appears only where the user's attention belongs: the active state, the playing progress, the current lyric line. The music is the subject and the chrome steps back. A single glow, the accent halo around the player card, is the one moment of spectacle.

Everything is the user's. The accent hue is a user setting, so the system is written in roles and alpha steps of "the accent", never in fixed hues. Reiatsu Violet is only the default.
keyCharacteristics: Dark, near-black canvas lit from behind by blurred album art.
Translucent obsidian glass surfaces tinted by the accent at low alpha (6–10%).
Softly rounded geometry everywhere; circles for the record and transport buttons.
Text hierarchy built from a ladder of white opacities, not from extra hues.
One accent halo, reserved for the player card.

rules.name: The User's Accent Rule
rules.body: Never hard-code a hue for an interactive or decorative element. Derive it from the theme primary with an alpha step: 0.06 (tint), 0.12–0.18 (hover/active fill), 0.25–0.35 (selected fill, borders) or 0.5+ (focus, emphasis).

rules.name: The White Ladder Rule
rules.body: Text hierarchy on dark surfaces is pure white for primary, 70% for labels and 60% for secondary and meta. Anything below 60% is for icons, disabled states and already-sung lyric lines, never for copy someone has to read.

rules.name: The Album Is the Light Rule
rules.body: In glass mode the backdrop is the current artwork blurred at sigma 65 under a 65% Abyss veil. Never replace it with a gradient or a stock texture. Opaque mode is flat Abyss.

rules.name: The Fixed Digits Rule
rules.body: Every time, duration and counter uses tabular figures, so ticking values never jitter.

rules.name: The Single Halo Rule
rules.body: The accent halo belongs to the player card and the hero Play button, nowhere else. Modals, dialogs and bars lift with neutral dark shadows only.

dos: Do derive every accent use from `colorScheme.primary` with the alpha steps of The User's Accent Rule.
Do keep text on the White Ladder: 100%, 70% or 60%.
Do use tabular figures for every time and count.
Do give every icon-only control a tooltip and a visible hover state.
Do keep every window state (empty, loading, error, detached) movable, closable and readable over arbitrary desktop content.
donts: Don't put the accent halo on anything except the player card and the hero Play button.
Don't hard-code surface colors in dialogs or modals (such as `#1A0B2E`). Use the theme's dialog and surface tokens.
Don't use readable copy below 60% white opacity.
Don't replace the blurred artwork backdrop with gradients or decorative textures.
Don't duplicate the same control in two places on one screen.
